title: Enforcement against cyclists and e-bike riders breaking road rules
asked: Whether the Ministry will work with the Ministry of Transport to step up enforcement against cyclists and e-bike users riding without helmets or lights, or against traffic, given the penalties motorists can face in accidents involving them.
response: Ms Sim Ann said the Traffic Police and LTA run regular enforcement at accident hotspots and locations reported by the public, and enforce against on-road cycling offences such as riding in groups of more than five, without helmets, without front and rear lights, and against the flow of traffic. On culpability, she said it is assessed holistically and that no one type of road user is always blamed disproportionately, with the whole situation of how an accident was caused looked into. She added that cyclists and e-bike users are treated like cars and other motorised vehicles on the roads, with similar enforcement.
